name: SYS_DEGRADE
title: Structural Erasure
description: Using the Sobel operator — an industrial computer vision tool — to reduce the human form to its mathematical edges, then re-weaving it into the ASCII character set. The project doesn't hide behind a 'filter.' It exposes the 1-bit dithering and the raw character grid. A study on how machines 'see' and 'remember' the user, moving from high-resolution surveillance to low-resolution archival texture.
abstract: Structural Erasure explores the boundary between human perception and computational memory. Through the Sobel edge-detection operator, human presence is reduced to gradient magnitudes — the mathematical skeleton of form. These edges are then mapped into the ASCII character set, a technology of the 1960s designed for teletype machines. The result is a real-time portrait that oscillates between recognition and abstraction, between surveillance and poetry. The work asks: when a machine remembers you, what does it choose to keep?

name: EFFECT_ROULETTE
title: Image Decomposition Engine
description: A systematic image decomposition pipeline. Upload any photograph and observe its destruction through seven algorithmic lenses: pixelation, voxelization, Floyd-Steinberg dithering, halftone screening, ASCII rendering, anaglyph displacement, and data-glitch corruption. Each effect exposes a different layer of the image's mathematical substrate.
abstract: EFFECT_ROULETTE treats every uploaded image as raw data to be dissected. Seven rendering modes — from the geometric purity of halftone dots to the entropic chaos of glitch slicing — each reveal what the image 'is' beneath the surface of human perception. The Floyd-Steinberg dithering algorithm, in particular, demonstrates how a continuous-tone photograph can be reduced to a single bit per pixel while preserving the illusion of depth through error diffusion.

name: CELLULAR_DITHER
title: Emergent Grid Automata
description: A cellular automaton driving a generative grid composition. Conway's Game of Life determines which cells live and die; the visual output renders each generation as a color-coded grid with multiple rulesets (Standard, HighLife, Day & Night, Seeds). The system oscillates between order and entropy — the grid as organism.
abstract: CELLULAR_DITHER collapses the distinction between algorithm and artwork. A cellular automaton — four simple rules governing birth and death — generates compositions that no human hand could predict. Each ruleset produces radically different emergent behavior: Standard Conway creates gliders and oscillators; HighLife spawns replicators; Day & Night produces organic, flowing patterns. The grid itself becomes a living system, its aesthetic value a byproduct of mathematical inevitability.
